assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Trent Ltd, consolidated, Rs crore. FY26 (Mar-2026) is the last reported year; Q1FY27 (Jun-2026, results 6-Aug-2026) is the last quarter known on 30-Sep-2026. Trent reports one segment (retail). We model revenue as a store build for the fashion business (Westside, Zudio and the small concepts, all in the listed company): effective retail area x revenue per sq ft of that area, plus the consolidated subsidiaries (consolidated less standalone: Zudio UAE, Booker wholesale, the Star stores held in Fiora Hypermarket, net of intra-group sales). Star (Trent Hypermarket, 50:50 with Tesco) and the Inditex associates (Zara 20%, Massimo Dutti) are equity-accounted: their share of profit sits in other income. The engine runs on revenueGrowth and ebitdaMargin; TRENT.ctx.js checks that the build below reproduces both exactly. Shares 53.32 cr after the 1:2 bonus (record date 4-Jun-2026); Screener EPS is restated for it. Minorities (Booker 49%) are tiny (Rs1.7 cr of FY26 profit).

build._note: Fashion retail area at year end: 17.7 mn sq ft at Mar-26 (300 Westside, 963 Zudio, 23 other stores), 18.04 mn at Jun-26 (1,312 stores; Q1FY27 presentation); 5.3 / 7.0 / 9.4 / 13.5 mn at Mar-22 to Mar-25 (AR FY26). Openings are back-ended (FY26 net adds by quarter 1 / 53 / 65 / 131; ~13.6 mn sq ft at Jun-25), so effective average area = opening area + 32% of the area added in the year (FY26: average of quarterly averages, with Sep-25 and Dec-25 area interpolated on net store adds, = 14.84 mn = 13.5 + 32% of 4.2). Revenue per effective sq ft FY26 = Rs19,701 cr / 14.84 mn = Rs13,276 (our measure); FY25 Rs15,560 on the same basis (16,668 / 10.71).
build._storeAddsWhy: Net fashion store additions. FY26: 272 opened (60 Westside, 212 Zudio), 22 consolidated, ~250 net; 'c.250 new stores a year' for the last few years (Q4FY26 presentation). AGM (23-Jun-2026, per Apparel Resources 24-Jun-2026): ~50 Westside and 200-250 Zudio a year, medium-term 700 Westside and ~5,000 Zudio. Q1FY27: 23 opened, 26 net incl. 6 other concepts; management: annual trajectory 'broadly consistent' with the AGM outlook. ICICI Direct (7-Aug-2026): ~49 Westside and 210-220 Zudio still to open in FY27.
build._sqftWhy: FY26 added 4.2 mn sq ft for ~250 net stores (16.8k each: Westside ~24k average, Zudio ~11k). We use 16k as the mix shifts to Zudio and smaller towns.
build._revPerSqftWhy: Revenue per effective sq ft fell ~15% in FY26 (Rs15,560 to Rs13,276) and ~10% y/y in Q1FY27 (Rs5,666 cr on ~17.9 mn sq ft vs Rs4,781 cr on ~13.55 mn; MOSL 6-Aug-2026 also -10%). Like-for-like growth was 'low single digits' in FY26 and Q1FY27 (company); >80% of new Zudio stores open in Tier II-III towns and peripheral micro-markets that 'mature over a two- to three-year period' (Q1FY27 presentation), and denser clusters cannibalise. Annualised FY26 sales per sq ft: Rs15,318 metro/Tier I, Rs13,390 Tier II, Rs12,504 rest of India (AR FY26). FY27E -8% (the FY26 cohort, 52% opened in Q4, ramps; mix keeps shifting to smaller towns), FY28E -1%, FY29E +1% as cohorts mature and LFL stays low single digit.
build._subsWhy: Consolidated less standalone revenue: Rs467 cr FY25, Rs373 cr FY26 (-20%), Rs89 cr in Q1FY27 (-13% y/y): Zudio UAE (7 stores; TGTL total income Rs61 cr, loss Rs14 cr), Booker wholesale (total income Rs199 cr), Star stores held in Fiora Hypermarket (Rs264 cr, down from Rs344 cr), net of intra-group sales (AR FY26 board report). FY27E -5%, then +5% a year. EBITDA Rs40 cr FY26, Rs8 cr Q1FY27: Rs35 / 40 / 45 cr.
build._marginWhy: Standalone EBITDA margin (Ind AS, Screener annual basis, bank charges in finance cost) 18.8% in FY26 (16.9% FY25; 18.5% on the quarterly basis). Q1FY27 19.6% (17.5% a year earlier): gross margin +149bp to 46.6% (ICICI Direct, MOSL) on mix and inventory health; operating EBITDA (pre-Ind AS) +36%. Management flags 'escalation in the cost levels of select inputs' (Q1FY27 presentation) and keeps prices stable. FY27E 19.3%, FY28E 19.5%, FY29E 19.6%. Subsidiaries' EBITDA Rs40 cr FY26, Rs8 cr Q1FY27.

assumptions._revenueWhy: From the store build (checked in TRENT.ctx.js). Q1FY27 consolidated revenue +17.9%, standalone +18.5%. Street: ICICI Direct FY27E Rs23,582 cr / FY28E Rs29,101 cr (7-Aug-2026); MOSL standalone revenue CAGR ~21% FY26-29E (6-Aug-2026).
assumptions._marginWhy: From the build: standalone EBITDA plus subsidiaries' EBITDA over consolidated revenue. FY26 18.7%, Q1FY27 19.4% (quarterly basis). See build._marginWhy.
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex here = cash capex plus cash lease payments (rent paid under Ind AS 116 shows up as lease repayment, not opex), so that free cash flow and the DCF are after rent. FY26: cash capex Rs1,737 cr (Screener: CFO 2,668 less FCF 931; the model history shows Screener's Rs1,763 cr) + payment of lease liabilities Rs797 cr (AR FY26 consolidated cash flow; Rs540 cr in FY25) = ~Rs2,530 cr; right-of-use additions were Rs1,242 cr (note 4). A new Zudio store needs Rs3-4 cr incl. capex, deposits and inventory (AR FY26). FY27E Rs1,900 + 950 cr, FY28E Rs2,100 + 1,100 cr, FY29E Rs2,300 + 1,250 cr. The Rs2,500 cr equity raise approved in principle on 22-Apr-2026 (store upgrades, new brands, warehousing, Star real estate) had not been launched by 30-Sep-2026 and is not modelled.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs1,361 cr (right-of-use amortisation ~Rs910 cr of it) = ~19% of the average gross block in the model; Q1FY27 Rs410 cr (7.1% of revenue, Rs1,640 cr annualised). 16% on the gross block gives Rs1.6k / 2.1k / 2.6k cr (6.8% / 7.3% / 7.7% of revenue): management says newer stores raise depreciation relative to revenue, but the engine also never retires assets, so the drift up is partly mechanical (see the report). CWIP (Rs254 cr) held flat.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: The engine's treasury is cash + investments less borrowings incl. Rs2,061 cr of lease liabilities, so it is negative (net debt incl. leases) and earns nothing; income on Trent's ~Rs1,150 cr of liquid funds is built into other income below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener 'other income' = reported other income + share of JVs/associates + exceptional items: FY26 Rs85 cr = 114.8 (AR FY26 consolidated note 29) + 3.9 (JV/associate share) - 26.1 (labour-code exceptional) - 7.6 (loss on assets discarded). Built: treasury income ~Rs55-65 cr (cash Rs281 cr, liquid funds Rs648 cr, bonds and G-secs Rs196 cr at Mar-26 less the Rs500 cr NCD repaid 29-May-2026, rebuilt by free cash) + unwinding of security deposits ~Rs30-40 cr (Rs28.6 cr FY26) + fair-value/sale gains and misc ~Rs20 cr + JV/associate share ~0-10 (Star loss share ~-Rs65 cr vs Zara/Massimo Dutti ~+Rs47 cr in FY26; FY26 total +Rs3.9 cr, FY25 +Rs86.5 cr). Screener quarters: Q1FY27 Rs30 cr; trailing four quarters Rs91 cr incl. the -Rs26 cr exceptional (Rs117 cr before it). FY27E Rs115 cr, FY28E Rs120 cr, FY29E Rs130 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (lease interest, NCD, bank charges)
assumptions._interestWhy: Screener annual finance cost Rs233 cr in FY26 = reported Rs168 cr (lease interest Rs134 cr, NCD Rs29 cr, other Rs5 cr; AR note 31) + ~Rs64 cr of bank charges Screener moves out of expenses. The 5.78% Rs500 cr NCD was repaid on 29-May-2026. Q1FY27 quarterly finance cost Rs47 cr. FY27E Rs245 cr (lease interest ~Rs165 cr, bank charges ~Rs75 cr, NCD ~Rs5 cr), FY28E Rs285 cr, FY29E Rs330 cr as the lease book grows ~15% a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 23.0% (Rs515 cr on Rs2,236 cr, incl. a Rs59 cr deferred-tax credit), FY25 24.4%, Q1FY27 25.1%. Standalone pays ~25% (new regime); JV/associate share is post-tax.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs6 per pre-bonus share (Rs4 post-bonus), Rs213 cr = 12% of profit; Trent pays 8-18%.

dcf._betaWhy: Discretionary fashion retail: earnings more cyclical than staples (DMart 0.75). Debt excluding leases is nil after the May-2026 NCD repayment; leases (~Rs2,100 cr) are ~1.5% of market value, so the cost of equity (12.2%) is the WACC.
dcf._tgWhy: Organised fashion and lifestyle retail in India is a ~Rs8-9 trn market with Trent at ~2% share (management, AGM 2026); a 6% nominal terminal rate (house range 5-6%) after 15 years of fade.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~19% (FY29E) to 10% over 15 years as the store base (1,300 now; ambition ~5,700) matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin (Ind AS, rent below EBITDA) fades to 18%: FY23-26 15-19%; leases keep rent out of EBITDA, so capex here includes right-of-use additions.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. right-of-use additions fades from ~12% of revenue (FY29E) to 7% as new stores fall relative to the base (lease renewals continue); depreciation incl. right-of-use 5.5% of revenue (FY26 6.8%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Zudio keeps opening 250+ stores a year and its Tier II-III cohorts ramp faster, like-for-like growth recovers to mid-to-high single digits, Westside steps up to ~100 openings a year, and gross margin holds at the Q1FY27 high.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Value fashion gets crowded (Reliance Yousta, Max, Style Union, Vishal, quick-commerce fashion), new stores in small towns stay unproductive, like-for-like growth turns negative, and input-cost inflation forces Trent to choose between price and margin.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Trent: the brokers that show their method use a sum of the parts in which Westside + Zudio are ~95% of value, on ~40x pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA (MOSL) or 64x Sep-28E P/E (Elara), and every target equals 58-64x FY28E EPS (MOSL 62x, Nuvama 58x at the CMP). Star and the Inditex stakes are inside consolidated EPS (equity-accounted). Multiple derived (TRENT.ctx.js): Trent one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 69.8x (no trough years; 69.8x also on EPS before the FY24 lease gain) x (1 - 29.6% retail-sector de-rating at 30-Sep-2026: DMart -21.8%, Metro Brands -29.1%, Bata -30.3%, Page -30.1%) = 49.1x, nearest half-turn 49x. Bull 70x (no de-rating); bear 32.5x (25th percentile 46.3x de-rated).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check (MOSL values Westside + Zudio on 40x pre-Ind AS EBITDA): Trent trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (60.2x, Screener, EV incl. lease liabilities) x the same sector factor x trailing-to-Sep-28E EBITDA (0.653) = 27.5x on Ind AS EBITDA, less net debt incl. leases.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether 15 years of store-led cash flows (after rent, via right-of-use additions in capex) support the price: FCFF at a 12.2% cost of capital, terminal growth 6%.

cover.headline: India's best fashion retailer, now growing by adding space faster than sales: still priced above what the de-rated sector justifies
cover.lead: Trent runs Zudio (982 value-fashion stores) and Westside (301 department stores), 18.0 mn sq ft in 330 cities at Jun-2026, all selling its own brands, plus equity-accounted stakes in Star (groceries, with Tesco) and Zara (with Inditex). Q1FY27 showed the new shape of growth: revenue +18% on ~33% more space, like-for-like growth "in the low single digits", a better gross margin, and profit +22% as depreciation rose 40%. We forecast EPS of ₹39.3 / ₹45.6 / ₹52.9 for FY27-29E (consolidated, post-bonus). The street's SOTPs boil down to **one-year-forward P/E** (58-64x FY28E). The house rule (Trent's forward P/E median since 2021, 69.8x, cut by the 29.6% de-rating of listed retailers) gives **49x Sep-28E EPS of ₹49.2 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**, close to the HOLD line. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹3,108; DCF ₹1,331. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A superb operator with a long runway
arguments.p: Own brands sold only in its own stores, an India-based supply chain and stable pricing gave Trent ~19% EBITDA margins and ~28% ROE while revenue grew ~34% a year over FY20-26. Management plans ~50 Westside and 200-250 Zudio stores a year towards ~700 and ~5,000; we model 250 / 260 / 270 net openings for FY27-29E (2,066 stores, 30.2 mn sq ft by FY29E).

arguments.h: But each sq ft now earns less
arguments.p: Revenue per effective sq ft fell from ₹15,560 in FY25 to ₹13,276 in FY26 and ~10% more in Q1FY27: like-for-like growth is low single digit, >80% of new Zudio stores open in smaller towns where sales per sq ft are ~18% below the metros, and Trent fills in its own catchments. We assume another −8% in FY27E, then roughly flat.

Rent on leased stores sits in depreciation and interest under Ind AS 116. Depreciation was 6.8% of revenue in FY26 and 7.1% in Q1FY27 (5.2% in FY25), so EBITDA +33% became profit +12% in FY26 (+22% in Q1). Star is still loss-making and a ₹2,500 cr equity raise is approved but not launched.

arguments.h: Valuation: the street pays for the old growth
arguments.p: At ₹2,622 Trent trades at 57.6x our FY28E and 53.3x Sep-28E EPS. Listed retailers were 29.6% below their five-year P/E medians on 30-Sep-2026; on the house rule Trent is worth 49x. The street's median target (₹3,536) uses 58-64x on higher standalone EPS. A DCF at a 12.2% cost of capital supports about half the price.

catalysts: Q2FY27 business update (early October) and results (due by mid-November 2026): store openings in the festive half and whether revenue per sq ft stops falling.
Festive and wedding season demand in H2FY27, against input-cost inflation that Trent is absorbing through sourcing and a "calibrated" price architecture.
The ₹2,500 cr equity raise: timing, route (rights issue or QIP) and price.
A new chairman after Noel Tata retires (he turns 70 in November 2026).
Competition in value fashion: Reliance's Yousta, Landmark's Max, Vishal Mega Mart and quick-commerce fashion in the towns Zudio is entering.

sections.title: Two own-brand fashion chains (Zudio and Westside) that own the shopper, the product and the store; Star and Zara on the side

blocks.p: Trent, the Tata group's retailer, sells fashion and lifestyle goods under its own brands in its own stores. **Zudio** (963 stores at Mar-26, 982 at Jun-26) is a value-fashion chain of 10,000-12,000 sq ft stores selling apparel, footwear and beauty at sharp price points, sourced almost entirely in India, with no discounting and little advertising; over 80% of new stores open in Tier II-III towns and the edges of big cities. **Westside** (300 stores, ~24,000 sq ft on average) is a department-store brand one notch up, with a growing online channel (over 6% of its revenue). Smaller concepts (Samoh, Burnt Toast) had 23 stores. Together the fashion business had 17.7 mn sq ft at Mar-26 and 18.0 mn sq ft at Jun-26 in 330 cities. Beauty, innerwear and footwear ("emerging categories") are over 21% of revenue.

The listed company (standalone) is the fashion business: ₹19,701 cr of revenue and ₹3,705 cr of EBITDA (18.8%) in FY26. Subsidiaries add only ₹373 cr net (Zudio UAE, Booker cash-and-carry, a few Star stores). Two businesses sit outside revenue because they are equity-accounted: **Star**, a food and grocery chain (86 stores at Jun-26) run by Trent Hypermarket, a 50:50 joint venture with Tesco, with ₹2,774 cr of income and a ₹128 cr pre-tax loss in FY26; and the **Inditex** associates that run Zara (Trent 20%, ₹2,768 cr of income, ₹204 cr of profit) and Massimo Dutti. Their net share of profit was just ₹3.9 cr in FY26 (₹86.5 cr in FY25): Star's loss now offsets Zara.

sections.title: From one Westside store to 1,300 fashion stores: Zudio changed the company; a bonus in 2026 and a raise approved

blocks.p: Trent started with Westside in 1998 and for two decades grew slowly; Zudio, launched in 2016, turned it into one of India's fastest-growing retailers after Covid. Food retail and the Zara stores were built with partners (Tesco and Inditex) and are equity-accounted, so the reported numbers are almost entirely Westside and Zudio. Per-share history needs one adjustment: the 1:2 bonus of June 2026 (35.55 cr to 53.32 cr shares); all EPS and prices in this report are on the post-bonus basis.

sections.title: Fashion and lifestyle: a ~₹12 lakh crore market growing ~12% a year, organised players faster, and value fashion getting crowded

blocks.p: India is the world's fourth-largest retail market, ~Rs90-95 lakh crore (~$1 trn) in CY2025, projected at ~Rs210-215 lakh crore by CY2035. Fashion and lifestyle (apparel, footwear, innerwear, beauty and personal care) was ~Rs12 lakh crore ($128 bn) in FY26 and is projected at ~Rs19 lakh crore by FY30 (~12% a year), with the organised part growing ~15% a year against ~9% for the unorganised part over FY25-30 (industry reports cited in AR FY26). Trent's FY26 revenue of ~Rs20,000 crore is ~1.7% of the fashion and lifestyle market; management puts its share at ~2% (AGM 2026).

bullets: **Categories.** Beauty and personal care ~Rs2.4 lakh crore in FY26 (Rs3.8 lakh crore by FY30), footwear ~Rs1.04 lakh crore (Rs1.6 lakh crore, ~11% a year), innerwear ~Rs84,000 crore (Rs1.3 lakh crore, ~12% a year) (AR FY26). These are Trent's 'emerging categories', now over 21% of its revenue.

**Competition.** Value fashion is crowded: Reliance Retail (Trends, Yousta), Landmark (Max), Vishal Mega Mart (listed Dec-2024), V-Mart, Aditya Birla (Pantaloons, Style Up) and Shoppers Stop (Intune) all run value formats; Zara, H&M and Uniqlo compete at the top. Trent says it has 'not witnessed any material shifts in the competitive intensity' (Q1FY27 presentation); brokers flag domestic and international fast fashion as the main risk (ICICI Direct, 7-Aug-2026).

**Smaller towns.** Over 80% of new Zudio stores open in Tier II-III towns and peripheral micro-markets; Trent's own data show lower sales per sq ft outside the metros (FY26: Rs15,318 metro/Tier I, Rs13,390 Tier II, Rs12,504 rest of India) and that new markets take two to three years to mature.

**Pricing.** Zudio keeps prices stable rather than discounting, and says it is calibrating its "price architecture" as input costs rise (Q1FY27). In value fashion, a few rupees on a low-priced T-shirt matter; there is little room to pass on inflation.

blocks.callout: **What matters for Trent:** the market is big enough for Zudio to keep growing at 20%+ in revenue for years on share gains alone (2% share today). The question is the quality of that growth: whether new stores in smaller towns reach the productivity of the old ones, and how much of Zudio's lead survives as Reliance, Landmark and Vishal copy the format.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the tailwind reaches Trent through new stores, not through the old ones. Like-for-like growth has been low single digit for over a year, so the company grows by adding space in smaller towns, where each sq ft earns less. That is still a profitable way to grow (a Zudio store needs only ₹3-4 cr of capital), but it is slower in profit than the store count suggests.

sections.title: The store engine: area up ~30% a year, revenue per sq ft down ~15% in FY26 and ~10% in Q1FY27

blocks.p: Trent grows by opening stores in clusters: it adds stores in catchments where it already trades (accepting some cannibalisation) and pushes into new towns. FY26 was the biggest year yet: 60 Westside and 212 Zudio stores opened, 22 closed or merged, 47 new cities; 131 of the ~250 net additions came in Q4. Q1FY27 added 20 net Westside and Zudio stores (plus 6 smaller concepts); management says the annual pace will stay in line with the AGM outlook of ~50 Westside and 200-250 Zudio stores a year, with medium-term targets of ~700 Westside and ~5,000 Zudio stores.

Productivity is the weak spot. On our measure (standalone revenue per sq ft of effective area, weighting new stores by the part of the year they were open), revenue per sq ft fell from ₹15,560 in FY25 to ₹13,276 in FY26 (−15%), and Q1FY27 revenue grew 18.5% on ~32% more average area (−10%, which MOSL also reports). Trent says like-for-like growth was "low single digits" in FY26 and Q1FY27, that new markets take two to three years to mature, and that it targets revenue growth per micro-market rather than per store. Its own data show the mix effect: FY26 annualised sales per sq ft were ₹15,318 in metro and Tier I cities, ₹13,390 in Tier II and ₹12,504 elsewhere, and most new space is in the last group.

sections.title: Star and Zara: ₹5,500 cr of sales outside the revenue line; Star's losses now cancel Zara's profit

blocks.p: **Star** (Trent Hypermarket, 50:50 with Tesco) runs 86 food and grocery stores in 12 cities (Jun-26), 18,000-24,000 sq ft, with own brands at 74% of sales and a Zudio shop-in-shop in most stores. Revenue (excl. GST) was ₹885 cr in Q1FY27, +9% y/y. THPL's total income was ₹2,774 cr in FY26 (+3%) and its loss before tax widened to ₹128 cr (₹92 cr in FY25) as stores were refitted and fruit and vegetable prices fell. Management says the business "increasingly delivers a viable economic profile at the store level" (Q1FY27) and plans 25-40 new stores a year; part of the proposed ₹2,500 cr raise is meant to speed this up, including retail real estate.

**Zara and Massimo Dutti** are run by Inditex with Trent as a minority partner: Trent owns 20% of Inditex Trent Retail India (Zara: ₹2,768 cr of income, −3%; profit ₹204 cr, down from ₹299 cr) and a stake in Massimo Dutti India (₹129 cr of income). Inditex controls sourcing and the brand licence (AR FY26). In FY26 Trent's net share of JV and associate profit was ₹3.9 cr (₹86.5 cr in FY25); Zara's dividends reach the standalone accounts, which is one reason standalone profit (₹1,968 cr) exceeds consolidated (₹1,721 cr).

blocks.callout: **So what:** in a sum of the parts the street adds Star at 2-2.5x sales (~₹50-65 a share for Trent's half) and Zara on ~40x P/E (~₹30 a share): together ~3% of value. Our P/E on consolidated EPS instead includes Star's losses (~₹1.2 a share); the difference is ~₹110-130 a share, which we show as a sensitivity. Neither stake changes the investment case; Star is an option that has not yet paid in a decade.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Trent is the best operator in Indian fashion retail: own brands, a fast supply chain and disciplined pricing gave it ~19% EBITDA margins and ~28% ROE while growing 30%+ a year. But that is an operating edge, not a moat that stops others: value fashion has low switching costs, and the biggest retailers in India are now copying Zudio. The edge shows in margins and returns; it does not protect same-store growth, which is already low single digit.

sections.title: Revenue 5.8x in six years and the margin up to ~19%, but depreciation is now growing faster than revenue

blocks.p: Trent's consolidated revenue was ₹3,486 cr in FY20 and ₹20,074 cr in FY26 (34% a year), almost all from Zudio's store roll-out (233 stores in FY22, 963 in FY26) and a steadier Westside. The EBITDA margin rose from 13.2% in FY22 to 18.7% in FY26 as scale, RFID-led manpower savings and a better gross margin came through. Two things make the profit line harder to read. FY24 profit (₹1,477 cr) includes a one-off ₹439 cr after-tax gain from reassessing lease terms, so FY25 growth looks flat. And rent sits below EBITDA under Ind AS 116: depreciation (mostly on leased stores) rose from ₹671 cr in FY24 to ₹1,361 cr in FY26 (6.8% of revenue, from 5.2%), so FY26 net profit grew 12% while EBITDA grew 33%.

sections.title: Self-funded growth on leased stores: high returns, but the cheque book is getting bigger (and a ₹2,500 cr raise is approved)

blocks.p: Trent leases almost all its stores, so the cash it puts into a new store is fit-out, deposits and inventory (₹3-4 cr for a Zudio), and rent is paid over the lease. That keeps returns high: ROE 28% in FY26 (32% in FY25; FY24's 44% was flattered by the one-off), and management reports operating ROCE of over 29%. Over FY22-26 operating cash was ₹6,331 cr and cash capex ₹4,542 cr; on top, lease payments were ₹797 cr in FY26 alone (₹540 cr in FY25), and right-of-use additions ₹1,242 cr. Dividends are modest (₹451 cr over FY22-26, ~9% of profit). In April 2026 the board approved in principle a ~₹2,500 cr equity raise (rights issue or otherwise) to speed up store upgrades, new brands, warehousing and automation, and Star's roll-out including real estate; it had not been launched by 30-Sep-2026. We do not model it: at the 30-Sep price it would add ~1.8% to the share count.

sections.title: The street after Q1: 11 of 15 positive, one Sell, targets ₹2,950-4,455, median ₹3,536

blocks.p: After the Q1FY27 results (6-Aug-2026) brokers raised targets on the margin beat. Motilal Oswal kept Buy at ₹3,775 (SOTP: 40x pre-Ind AS EBITDA for Westside and Zudio; ~62x FY28E EPS); ICICI Direct Buy ₹3,599 (SOTP); Elara Accumulate ₹3,500 (64x Sep-28E standalone P/E, Star 2x EV/Sales, Zara 40x P/E); Nuvama Buy ₹3,591 (from ₹3,219); UBS Buy ₹3,800; Macquarie Outperform ₹3,600; Antique ₹4,455 at the top; Goldman Sachs Neutral ₹3,000 and Citi Sell ₹2,950 at the bottom. Median of the 15: ₹3,536, +35% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹2,622; Business Today's consensus target was ₹3,454. The brokers that disclose a method use a sum of the parts: Westside and Zudio on ~40x pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA (MOSL) or ~64x Sep-28E P/E (Elara), plus Star on 2-2.5x sales and the Zara/Massimo Dutti stakes on P/E. The fashion business is ~95% of each SOTP, and the overall targets equal ~58-64x FY28E EPS (MOSL 62x, Nuvama 58x at the CMP), on standalone EPS that is ~10-15% above consolidated EPS (no Star losses; dividends from the Inditex associates).

exhibit.title: Critiques we take seriously
head: Argument
rows: Growth is bought with space: area grew ~31% in FY26 and ~33% y/y to Jun-26 while revenue grew 15-19%; like-for-like growth has been low single digit for over a year, so revenue per sq ft fell ~15% in FY26 and ~10% in Q1FY27.

New stores in smaller towns are less productive (annualised sales per sq ft Rs12,504 outside Tier I-II vs Rs15,318 in metros) and Trent opens next to its own stores: cannibalisation is a deliberate choice that the reported LFL cannot show.

Depreciation is rising faster than revenue (6.8% of revenue in FY26, 7.1% in Q1FY27, 5.2% in FY25): under Ind AS 116 rent sits below EBITDA, so EBITDA growth (+32% in Q1) overstates profit growth (+22%).
Star (THPL) is still loss-making after a decade (Rs128 cr loss before tax in FY26, wider than FY25) and part of the Rs2,500 cr raise is earmarked to roll it out faster.
A Rs2,500 cr equity raise (~1.8% of the market value) is approved but not launched: an overhang, and a sign that internal cash no longer covers every ambition.

Value fashion is getting crowded (Reliance's Yousta, Landmark's Max, Vishal, V-Mart) and quick-commerce platforms now sell basic apparel: Zudio's price advantage is harder to defend than its execution.
The stock still trades at ~53x our Sep-28E EPS after halving from its Oct-2024 peak: the street's 58-64x on FY28E assumes ~20% EPS growth for many years.
exhibit.source: Company documents and broker notes as cited; GAM Research

sections.title: Our honest summary: an excellent retailer at a price that still assumes the old growth; SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's best-run fashion retailer, with own brands, a fast supply chain, ~19% EBITDA margins and ~28% ROE, adding ~250 stores a year with a clear runway (management talks of ~5,000 Zudio stores). Growth has become space-led: like-for-like sales are growing in low single digits, revenue per sq ft fell ~15% in FY26 and ~10% in Q1FY27, and depreciation is outgrowing revenue. Star is still loss-making, Zara's profit fell, and a ₹2,500 cr equity raise is pending.

**What you are paying:** 66.7x our FY27E and 57.6x FY28E EPS. Trent's own forward P/E has a median of 69.8x since 2021; listed retailers were 29.6% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026, which gives 49x Sep-28E EPS and {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): SELL on our rule. EV/EBITDA (₹3,108) is higher because Ind AS EBITDA outgrows profit; a DCF at a 12.2% cost of capital (₹1,331) is far below. The street (median ₹3,536) sees ~35% upside; we think it is paying for a growth rate the store economics no longer deliver.

build._note: Fashion retail area at year end: 17.7 mn sq ft at Mar-26 (300 Westside, 963 Zudio, 23 other stores), 18.04 mn at Jun-26 (1,312 stores; Q1FY27 presentation); 5.3 / 7.0 / 9.4 / 13.5 mn at Mar-22 to Mar-25 (AR FY26). Revenue per effective sq ft FY26 = Rs19,701 cr / 14.84 mn = Rs13,276 (our measure); FY25 Rs15,560 on the same basis (16,668 / 10.71).

AGM (23-Jun-2026, per Apparel Resources 24-Jun-2026): ~50 Westside and 200-250 Zudio a year, medium-term 700 Westside and ~5,000 Zudio. Annualised FY26 sales per sq ft: Rs15,318 metro/Tier I, Rs13,390 Tier II, Rs12,504 rest of India (AR FY26). FY27E -8% (the FY26 cohort, 52% opened in Q4, ramps; mix keeps shifting to smaller towns), FY28E -1%, FY29E +1% as cohorts mature and LFL stays low single digit.

assumptions._capexWhy: Capex here = cash capex plus cash lease payments (rent paid under Ind AS 116 shows up as lease repayment, not opex), so that free cash flow and the DCF are after rent. FY26: cash capex Rs1,737 cr (Screener: CFO 2,668 less FCF 931; the model history shows Screener's Rs1,763 cr) + payment of lease liabilities Rs797 cr (AR FY26 consolidated cash flow; Rs540 cr in FY25) = ~Rs2,530 cr; right-of-use additions were Rs1,242 cr (note 4). A new Zudio store needs Rs3-4 cr incl. capex, deposits and inventory (AR FY26). FY27E Rs1,900 + 950 cr, FY28E Rs2,100 + 1,100 cr, FY29E Rs2,300 + 1,250 cr. The Rs2,500 cr equity raise approved in principle on 22-Apr-2026 (store upgrades, new brands, warehousing, Star real estate) had not been launched by 30-Sep-2026 and is not modelled.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs1,361 cr (right-of-use amortisation ~Rs910 cr of it) = ~19% of the average gross block in the model; Q1FY27 Rs410 cr (7.1% of revenue, Rs1,640 cr annualised). 16% on the gross block gives Rs1.6k / 2.1k / 2.6k cr (6.8% / 7.3% / 7.7% of revenue): management says newer stores raise depreciation relative to revenue, but the engine also never retires assets, so the drift up is partly mechanical (see the report). CWIP (Rs254 cr) held flat.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: The engine's treasury is cash + investments less borrowings incl. Rs2,061 cr of lease liabilities, so it is negative (net debt incl. leases) and earns nothing; income on Trent's ~Rs1,150 cr of liquid funds is built into other income below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener 'other income' = reported other income + share of JVs/associates + exceptional items: FY26 Rs85 cr = 114.8 (AR FY26 consolidated note 29) + 3.9 (JV/associate share) - 26.1 (labour-code exceptional) - 7.6 (loss on assets discarded). Built: treasury income ~Rs55-65 cr (cash Rs281 cr, liquid funds Rs648 cr, bonds and G-secs Rs196 cr at Mar-26 less the Rs500 cr NCD repaid 29-May-2026, rebuilt by free cash) + unwinding of security deposits ~Rs30-40 cr (Rs28.6 cr FY26) + fair-value/sale gains and misc ~Rs20 cr + JV/associate share ~0-10 (Star loss share ~-Rs65 cr vs Zara/Massimo Dutti ~+Rs47 cr in FY26; FY26 total +Rs3.9 cr, FY25 +Rs86.5 cr). Screener quarters: Q1FY27 Rs30 cr; trailing four quarters Rs91 cr incl. the -Rs26 cr exceptional (Rs117 cr before it). FY27E Rs115 cr, FY28E Rs120 cr, FY29E Rs130 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (lease interest, NCD, bank charges)
assumptions._interestWhy: Screener annual finance cost Rs233 cr in FY26 = reported Rs168 cr (lease interest Rs134 cr, NCD Rs29 cr, other Rs5 cr; AR note 31) + ~Rs64 cr of bank charges Screener moves out of expenses. The 5.78% Rs500 cr NCD was repaid on 29-May-2026. Q1FY27 quarterly finance cost Rs47 cr. FY27E Rs245 cr (lease interest ~Rs165 cr, bank charges ~Rs75 cr, NCD ~Rs5 cr), FY28E Rs285 cr, FY29E Rs330 cr as the lease book grows ~15% a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 23.0% (Rs515 cr on Rs2,236 cr, incl. a Rs59 cr deferred-tax credit), FY25 24.4%, Q1FY27 25.1%. Standalone pays ~25% (new regime); JV/associate share is post-tax.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs6 per pre-bonus share (Rs4 post-bonus), Rs213 cr = 12% of profit; Trent pays 8-18%.

dcf._betaWhy: Discretionary fashion retail: earnings more cyclical than staples (DMart 0.75). Debt excluding leases is nil after the May-2026 NCD repayment; leases (~Rs2,100 cr) are ~1.5% of market value, so the cost of equity (12.2%) is the WACC.
dcf._tgWhy: Organised fashion and lifestyle retail in India is a ~Rs8-9 trn market with Trent at ~2% share (management, AGM 2026); a 6% nominal terminal rate (house range 5-6%) after 15 years of fade.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~19% (FY29E) to 10% over 15 years as the store base (1,300 now; ambition ~5,700) matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin (Ind AS, rent below EBITDA) fades to 18%: FY23-26 15-19%; leases keep rent out of EBITDA, so capex here includes right-of-use additions.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. right-of-use additions fades from ~12% of revenue (FY29E) to 7% as new stores fall relative to the base (lease renewals continue); depreciation incl. right-of-use 5.5% of revenue (FY26 6.8%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Zudio keeps opening 250+ stores a year and its Tier II-III cohorts ramp faster, like-for-like growth recovers to mid-to-high single digits, Westside steps up to ~100 openings a year, and gross margin holds at the Q1FY27 high.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Value fashion gets crowded (Reliance Yousta, Max, Style Union, Vishal, quick-commerce fashion), new stores in small towns stay unproductive, like-for-like growth turns negative, and input-cost inflation forces Trent to choose between price and margin.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Trent: the brokers that show their method use a sum of the parts in which Westside + Zudio are ~95% of value, on ~40x pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA (MOSL) or 64x Sep-28E P/E (Elara), and every target equals 58-64x FY28E EPS (MOSL 62x, Nuvama 58x at the CMP). Star and the Inditex stakes are inside consolidated EPS (equity-accounted). Multiple derived (TRENT.ctx.js): Trent one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 69.8x (no trough years; 69.8x also on EPS before the FY24 lease gain) x (1 - 29.6% retail-sector de-rating at 30-Sep-2026: DMart -21.8%, Metro Brands -29.1%, Bata -30.3%, Page -30.1%) = 49.1x, nearest half-turn 49x. Bull 70x (no de-rating); bear 32.5x (25th percentile 46.3x de-rated).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check (MOSL values Westside + Zudio on 40x pre-Ind AS EBITDA): Trent trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (60.2x, Screener, EV incl. lease liabilities) x the same sector factor x trailing-to-Sep-28E EBITDA (0.653) = 27.5x on Ind AS EBITDA, less net debt incl. leases.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether 15 years of store-led cash flows (after rent, via right-of-use additions in capex) support the price: FCFF at a 12.2% cost of capital, terminal growth 6%.
